name: Bandit
hardware_needs: Light static analyser (AST-based)
integration_role: Python-specific insecure-pattern detection: eval/exec, subprocess with shell=True, hardcoded passwords, unsafe deserialisation, weak crypto
samx_problem: If SAM-X ever runs model-produced or downloaded code, the FIRST control is to know exactly where that happens in the codebase. Bandit finds those sites mechanically.
what_inspected: README.rst, bandit/ layout, LICENSE (Apache-2.0); pushed 2026-10-12
limitations: AST pattern matching: high false-negative rate for logic flaws; it cannot reason about data flow from an untrusted document to a dangerous sink. Findings are leads, not guarantees.
fallback: A documented manual audit of every eval/exec/subprocess/pickle call site, with a rule that untrusted content may never reach them.
experiment: Run Bandit over the SAM-X codebase (authorised separately) and triage: produce a table of every dynamic-execution site, whether untrusted content can reach it, and the mitigation. Label all mitigations as proposed until demonstrated.

name: bitsandbytes

what_inspected: Bundled docs/source/features/{quantization,8bitoptimizers}.md, index.md; README.md; LICENSE (MIT); pushed 2026-09-07

fallback: GGUF quantisation via llama.cpp (CPU-friendly) or a smaller unquantised model.
experiment: Same model, two quantisation levels, on 30 frozen field-extraction items: measure exact-field accuracy, negation/exception recall, RSS and tokens/s. Reject a quantisation level if accuracy drops more than the pre-declared tolerance.

(arXiv:2310.01798 — id NOT re-verified this session) LLMs cannot reliably self-correct reasoning without external feedback. Reflexion gains in the paper come from environments with ground-truth signals (HumanEval, ALFWorld). Without an independent checker, a reflection can encode a WRONG lesson permanently.
